items.stem: What does ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY date) produce?

options.text: A sequential number restarting at 1 within each customer, ordered by date
options.rationale: PARTITION BY resets numbering per group; ORDER BY sets the sequence.

options.text: A single number for the whole result set
options.rationale: PARTITION BY restarts the count per partition.

options.text: The same rank for tied dates
options.rationale: ROW_NUMBER is always distinct; RANK handles ties.

options.text: A running sum of a column
options.rationale: ROW_NUMBER numbers rows; it does not sum.

items.explanation: PARTITION BY resets numbering per group; ORDER BY sets the sequence.

items.stem: Select TWO correct statements about UNION versus UNION ALL.

options.text: UNION removes duplicate rows across the combined results
options.rationale: UNION performs a distinct operation on the union.

options.text: UNION ALL keeps all rows including duplicates and is usually cheaper
options.rationale: UNION ALL skips the dedup step, saving work.

options.text: UNION ALL sorts the result by the first column
options.rationale: Neither guarantees ordering without ORDER BY.

options.text: UNION requires the inputs to have different column counts
options.rationale: Both require matching column counts and compatible types.

items.explanation: UNION performs a distinct operation on the union.

items.stem: Why can a recursive CTE be the right tool for hierarchical data?

options.text: It can repeatedly join a table to itself to traverse parent-child levels
options.rationale: The recursive member walks the hierarchy until no new rows are produced.

options.text: It automatically creates indexes on the hierarchy
options.rationale: A CTE does not create indexes.

options.text: It is the only way to filter rows
options.rationale: Filtering uses WHERE; recursion is about traversal.

options.text: It guarantees better performance than any join
options.rationale: Recursion is about expressiveness, not guaranteed speed.

items.explanation: The recursive member walks the hierarchy until no new rows are produced.
